title: O Thou, Whose Presence Went Before
description: O Thou, Whose Presence Went Before in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Greenleaf Whittier wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 435, “The Day of Freedom”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou, whose pre-sence went be-fore Our fa-thers in their wea-ry way, As with Thy cho-sen moved of yore The fire by night, the cloud by day!

lines: O Thou, whose presence went before
Our fathers in their weary way,
As with Thy chosen moved of yore
The fire by night, the cloud by day!
When, from each temple of the free,
A nation's song ascends to heaven,
Most holy Father, unto Thee
Now let our humble prayer be given.
Sweet peace be here; and hope and love
Be round us as a mantle thrown,
As unto Thee, supreme above,
The knee of prayer is bowed alone.
And grant, O Father, that the time
Of earth's deliverance may be near,
When every land, and tongue, and clime,
The message of Thy love shall hear; —
When, smitten as with fire from heaven,
The captive's chain shall sink in dust,
And to his fettered soul be given
The glorious freedom of the just.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Greenleaf Whittier died in 1892.
credits: Words by John Greenleaf Whittier (1807–1892), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
